summary: Created src/tests/workspace-health.test.ts with 8 unit tests for checkWorkspaceHealth().

Tests cover: fully healthy workspace, missing .code-workspace file, one uncloned repo, multiple uncloned repos, both issues simultaneously, empty repo list (healthy + file missing), and .git file vs directory semantics.
All temp directories are created under a single top-level tmpRoot and cleaned up via process.on('exit').
Each test asserts exact field values (type, severity, fixAction, repositoryId, message presence) on the returned WorkspaceHealthReport.
No network access — all tests operate entirely on the local filesystem using temp directories.
707/707 total tests pass.

comments.note: test `'.git file (not directory) does not satisfy the cloned check'` documents that `fs.existsSync` returns true for both files and directories, meaning a git worktree pointer file (`.git` as a file) passes the cloned check. This is consistent with the current implementation but worth reviewing if the project ever needs to distinguish between full clones and worktrees.

The helper `wsFilePath()` duplicates the logic of `getWorkspaceFilePath()` from vscode-workspace.ts. This is intentional (keeping the test self-contained), but if the path convention ever changes, the test helper must be updated too.
8 tests cover all current check types plus edge cases (empty repo list, multiple issues, .git file vs directory). Coverage is complete for the current implementation.

summary: Reviewed src/tests/workspace-health.test.ts. PASS with one Fix-Forward applied.

Fix-Forward: assert.ok(report.issues.length >= 2) → assert.strictEqual(report.issues.length, 2) in the both-problems test. The setup creates exactly one file-missing condition and one uncloned-repo condition; the exact count is 2. The >= 2 form was under-constrained.

Test coverage is comprehensive: 8 scenarios covering healthy, file-missing, single repo missing, multiple repos missing, both issues, empty repo list (healthy + file missing), and .git file vs directory edge case.
Cleanup pattern: single tmpRoot + process.on('exit') + fs.rmSync recursive — correct per AGENTS.md constraints. Each test uses isolated makeTempDir() subdirectory.
wsFilePath helper duplication is intentional and documented — correct tradeoff for test self-containment.
One documentation-forward (low): .git file/dir dual behavior should be noted in module JSDoc.

comments.note: In 'returns both workspace-file-missing and repository-not-cloned when both problems exist' test (line ~150): changed assert.ok(report.issues.length >= 2) to assert.strictEqual(report.issues.length, 2). The test creates exactly one missing-file condition and one uncloned-repo condition, so the expected count is precisely 2. The >= 2 form was under-constrained — it would pass even if checkWorkspaceHealth returned spurious extra issues. Non-behavioral change (no production code touched).

Test file structure is excellent: single tmpRoot with process.on('exit') cleanup as required by AGENTS.md, each test uses an isolated makeTempDir() subdirectory, all assertions use node:assert/strict. 8 tests cover a complete scenario matrix for checkWorkspaceHealth.

The wsFilePath helper duplication is intentional and correctly documented inline. Keeping the test self-contained is the right tradeoff — importing the production helper would create an implicit coupling between the test and implementation internals.

[documentation-forward] The .git file vs .git directory edge case test (last test) documents non-obvious behavior: fs.existsSync returns true for both, so git worktree pointers are treated as cloned. This behavioral characteristic should be noted in workspace-health.ts module JSDoc or in gui-frontend.md so future contributors don't inadvertently change the check to isDirectory without understanding the implications.
